subject: Deployment fabric guardrails and threat journey
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@highlandmutual.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@highlandmutual.com
Date: 2026-10-11T14:12:00Z
Subject: Highland Mutual RFP: network/topology questions and diagrams request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this RFP. As part of our security questionnaire we'd like to capture two artifacts for our internal reviewers: a high-level topology diagram showing trust boundaries (control plane, data plane, operator plane) and a short description of your isolation model (how tenant inference traffic, control-plane metadata, and telemetry are segmented).

Could you also include a short threat-summary (2-3 pages or bullets) that explains the primary attack paths you consider for tenant egress or KV cache leakage, and the mitigations you rely on (sidecar egress controls, HSM/KMS separation, etc.)? Our deadline to include code in the procurement packet is EOD Oct 14 PT.

If there are standard artifacts you provide (diagram + matrix + evidence PDF) we can accept those — preferably PDF/PNG/XLSX. Alicia from our SI will be reviewing for architecture.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Senior Security Engineer
Highland Mutual

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@highlandmutual.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <agomez@consult-sols.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Highland Mutual RFP: network/topology questions and diagrams request

Daniel — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching the artifacts you requested and a short narrative.

Attachments: redwood-deployment-fabric-diagram-v2.png (schematic), threat-scenario-matrix.xlsx, segmentation-proof-points.pdf

Summary (topline):
- Topology: Redwood separates runtime into three logical planes: Control (control plane APIs, model registry), Data (inference runtime + KV cache), and Operator (management agents, autoscaler). Networking is implemented with per-tenant overlay + per-cluster sealed subnets — see diagram.
- Isolation model: Network segmentation is enforced via per-tenant VPCs (customer-provided VPC for Private; dedicated subnets for Dedicated) and strict egress policies at the sidecar. Each GPU pod hosts a sidecar proxy that mediates egress and enforces allowlists and mTLS to internal destinations.
- Threat summary (high level): primary concerns are prefix leakage from KV cache, sidecar misconfiguration leading to outbound exfil, and control-plane token misuse. Mitigations: ephemeral KMS-backed keys for token issuance, KV cache encryption-at-rest + per-tenant cache namespaces, continuous egress policy validation with split-gate fail-closed behavior.

We also included a short evidence packet (segmentation-proof-points.pdf) that lists audit log locations, examples of per-tenant telemetry, and a sample network ACL policy. If you want, we can provide a short recorded walkthrough and the layered attack matrix in spreadsheet form.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Security
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Highland Mutual RFP: network/topology questions and diagrams request

Daniel / Alicia — following up with the clarifications Kim requested and a slightly expanded threat narrative embedded below. I've attached the KMS rotation artifact sample and a short cache eviction note in segmentation-proof-points.pdf.

Key clarifications: 
- Fail mode: For Dedicated and Private deployments our sidecar enforces a fail-closed posture for outbound flows. For Redwood Hosted we implement policy-safeguard circuit breakers: under control-plane degradation, requests are routed to a hardened fallback model with outbound blocks unless allowlisted by exception documented in the SLA.
- KMS audit evidence: included (segmentation-proof-points.pdf) — sample rotation timestamps, key-id fingerprints, and audit log paths.
- KV cache tenancy: we use per-tenant namespaces keyed by tenant-id; on eviction we zero memory pages and rotate per-tenant cache encryption keys. The evidence PDF contains a one-paragraph technical description and a snippet of our eviction flow.

Expanded threat journey (concise):
1) Scenario: Prefix leakage via inadvertent KV namespace collision
   - Likelihood: low (namespaces enforced at cache API + runtime enforcement)
   - Impact: medium-high (could leak short-term conversational prefixes)
   - Controls: namespace validation in control plane, per-tenant encryption keys, post-creation integration tests, and runtime assertions recorded in telemetry.

2) Scenario: Sidecar misroute/exfiltration from operator mistake
   - Likelihood: medium (human config error is plausible)
   - Impact: high
   - Controls: declarative network policy templates, automated policy linting during rollout, role-segregated deploys, and an egress proof harness executed daily that verifies allowlists.

3) Scenario: Control-plane token compromise
   - Likelihood: low-to-medium (mitigated by ephemeral creds)
   - Impact: high
   - Controls: short-lived signed tokens (rotate per-call where required), HSM-backed KMS for root keys, and replay protection in RPC server.

If this level of detail is sufficient we'll mark the RFP packet as "technical appendix included" and share a 30-minute walkthrough with your SI. Otherwise we can expand the matrix into a 6-page threat narrative.

Attachments in this message: redwood-deployment-fabric-diagram-v2.png, threat-scenario-matrix.xlsx, segmentation-proof-points.pdf
